successors.name: Kingdom of the Franks
successors.text: the duchy of Bavaria, incorporated after Tassilo III's deposition

ledger.x: 540: the Bavarii, first named 'by about 520', appear as a people on the Danube and the northern Alps (Cliopatria's start); the duchy proper begins about 555.
546: a few edge cells are added to the Bavarian shape (Cliopatria).

c. 555: Garibald I, first documented duke, rules the Bavarians as an Agilolfing duke under Merovingian overlordship. 'ruled from 555 onward as a largely independent Merovingian vassal'; infobox 'c. 555-788'; the Agilolfings page lists him from 548, the Garibald page 'from 555 until 591'.
555: the Alpine edge is added to the shape (Cliopatria; 14 of its 15 cells lay in the Ostrogothic shape of 550).
633: Samo's Slavic union takes the eastern fringe of Bavaria (Cliopatria; 27 of the 30 cells lie in its 640 shape).
661: part of the fringe returns to Bavaria after Samo's union ends ('Samo's death in 658 or 659'); the rest becomes Carantania.

c. 743: Duke Odilo makes the Slavic princes of Carantania his vassals. 'At around 743, the Bavarian duke Odilo vassalised the Slavic princes of Carantania'; the Carantania page has Boruth ask Odilo for help against the Avars 'about 740' and lists the principality as a 'tributary to Franks: 745', so the Franks share…
788: with the duchy absorbed by the Franks, the Bavarian overlordship of Carantania ends and the Frankish one remains (integration into the Frankish realm follows in 828).
788: Charlemagne deposes Tassilo III and Bavaria is absorbed into the Frankish kingdom.

wars.name: Frankish-Bavarian war of 743
wars.outcome: Odilo, who 'rebelled to support the Alamans with the support of Hunald I of Aquitaine in 742/43', was 'defeated in 743 after a battle at the river Lech' and 'had to accept Frankish overlordship over Bavaria, but remained duke'.

wars.name: Odilo's intervention in Carantania
wars.outcome: Odilo 'came to the aid of Prince Boruth of Carantania against repeated Avar incursions' and 'was able to vassalize the Slavic principality in the southeast'.

wars.name: Avar incursion into Bavaria of 788
wars.outcome: 'Already in 788, the Avars made an incursion into Bavaria', where 'the Avars suffered a significant defeat (788)'; the eastern Bavarian border towards the Avars then lay on the Enns.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on the pages opened.
